descriptor: Georgia's capital in a valley on the Mtkvari River, sheltered by the Caucasus on either side.

name: Bogotá
descriptor: On a high Andean plateau — near-constant spring-like temperatures year-round, latitude notwithstanding.

name: Medellín
descriptor: Known as the "City of Eternal Spring" for its mild, remarkably stable Andean valley climate.

name: Quito
descriptor: The second-highest capital city in the world, almost exactly on the equator yet cool from elevation alone.

name: La Paz
descriptor: The world's highest administrative capital, over 3,600m up in the Andes — thin air, huge daily swings.

name: Addis Ababa
descriptor: One of Africa's highest capitals, its elevation giving it mild temperatures despite a near-equatorial latitude.

name: Mexico City
descriptor: In a high valley ringed by volcanoes — elevation keeps it far cooler than its latitude suggests.

name: Cusco
descriptor: The old Inca capital, high in the Andes with thin air and sharp day-night temperature swings.

name: Arequipa
descriptor: Below a volcano at over 2,300m, sunny and dry nearly year-round.

name: Kathmandu
descriptor: Nepal's capital in a Himalayan valley, its climate a world apart from the peaks visible from it.

name: Thimphu
descriptor: One of the world's highest capitals, tucked in a Himalayan valley with cold, dry winters.

name: Johannesburg
descriptor: South Africa's largest city, high on the Highveld plateau, with crisp winters and thunderstorm summers.

name: Nairobi
descriptor: Nearly 1,800m up on the East African plateau — famously temperate despite sitting almost on the equator.

name: Kigali
descriptor: Rwanda's hilly capital, mild year-round thanks to its highland elevation.

name: Lhasa
descriptor: The highest major city in the world, on the Tibetan Plateau — thin, dry, intensely sunny air.

name: Leh
descriptor: A cold desert town high in the Indian Himalayas, cut off from monsoon moisture by the mountains around it.

name: Bengaluru
descriptor: India's tech capital, on the Deccan Plateau — famously milder than the tropical coasts on either side.

name: Sucre
descriptor: Bolivia's constitutional capital, lower and notably milder than La Paz further up the altiplano.

name: Antananarivo
descriptor: Madagascar's capital on the central highlands, cooler than the tropical coasts that ring the island.

name: San José
descriptor: In Costa Rica's Central Valley, its elevation buying near-perpetual mild "eternal spring" weather.

name: Tegucigalpa
descriptor: Honduras's capital in a mountain valley, milder than the tropical coast.

name: Guatemala City
descriptor: On a high volcanic plateau — locally known for weather closer to eternal spring than tropical heat.

name: Guadalajara
descriptor: On a high plateau in western Mexico, mild for its latitude thanks to elevation.

name: Asmara
descriptor: On a highland plateau at over 2,300m — one of the mildest capitals anywhere near the equator.

name: Sana'a
descriptor: One of the highest capital cities in the world, in the Yemeni highlands with genuinely cool nights.

name: Kabul
descriptor: High in a Hindu Kush valley — cold, snowy winters unusual for its latitude.

name: Honolulu
descriptor: Hawai'i's capital, kept remarkably stable year-round by the surrounding Pacific and trade winds.

name: Suva
descriptor: Fiji's capital, warm and humid with a wetter season through the Southern Hemisphere summer.

name: Papeete
descriptor: Tahiti's main town, warm and humid year-round with a wetter November-to-April season.

name: Nassau
descriptor: Warmed and cooled by the surrounding Atlantic — hurricane season is the real seasonal event here.

name: Port Louis
descriptor: On a coral-fringed Indian Ocean island, warm year-round with a summer cyclone risk.

name: Malé
descriptor: One of the lowest-lying capitals on Earth — a coral atoll where the ocean sets almost every condition.

name: Funchal
descriptor: Madeira's capital, kept remarkably mild all year by the surrounding Atlantic.

name: Hamilton
descriptor: A mid-Atlantic island, warmed by the Gulf Stream well north of the tropics.

name: Apia
descriptor: Samoa's capital, warm year-round with a wetter season and real cyclone risk in the Southern summer.

name: Port Vila
descriptor: A South Pacific island capital, in the path of the region's cyclone season each year.

name: Majuro
descriptor: A low coral atoll in the central Pacific — among the most exposed inhabited places to sea-level rise.

name: Nuku'alofa
descriptor: Tonga's capital, warm year-round with real tropical cyclone risk each Southern summer.

name: Saint-Denis
descriptor: On a volcanic Indian Ocean island, warm coasts giving way to a much cooler, wetter interior.

name: Praia
descriptor: On a volcanic Atlantic archipelago, dry for its tropical latitude thanks to a cool offshore current.

name: Bridgetown
descriptor: The easternmost Caribbean island — first in line for tropical waves crossing the Atlantic.

name: Charlotte Amalie
descriptor: A Caribbean harbour town, warm year-round with real hurricane exposure.

name: Stanley
descriptor: A remote South Atlantic outpost, cool, windy and changeable nearly every day of the year.

name: Nouméa
descriptor: A South Pacific capital on a lagoon, warm year-round with a summer cyclone season.

name: Victoria
descriptor: One of the smallest national capitals on Earth, on a granite island just south of the equator.
